title: am / are / is (I, you, it)
uz: To be: I am, you are, it is
focus: Verb to be with I, you, it and names: I'm Ben. You're Mika. My name's ... This is ... Contractions I'm, you're, it's, what's. Questions What's your name? How are you?
parts: Darak gaplar (I am / you are / it is)

title: Possessive adjectives: my, your
focus: my and your before nouns: my name, your book, my bag. What's your name? My name is ...

title: Plural nouns (-s, -es)
focus: Regular plurals: book-books, camera-cameras; -es after s, ss, sh, ch, x: bus-buses, sandwich-sandwiches, watch-watches. Numbers + plural nouns: two books.

title: am / are / is (he, she, they)
uz: To be: he is, she is, they are
focus: He's / She's / It's / They're with jobs, places and countries: He's from Brazil. She's a student. They're in New York. Contractions.

title: Possessive adjectives: his, her
focus: his (for a man) and her (for a woman): His name's Pablo. What's her name? Difference between he's (he is) and his.
parts: he's yoki his? she's yoki her?

title: Questions with what, where, how
focus: What's your/his/her name? Where are you from? Where is she from? How are you? How old are you? Word order: question word + be + subject.

title: Verb to be: negatives
uz: To be: inkor (I'm not, isn't, aren't)
focus: I'm not, he/she/it isn't, we/you/they aren't. I'm not a teacher. She isn't married. They aren't from Spain.

title: Verb to be: questions and short answers
uz: To be: so'roq gaplar va qisqa javoblar
focus: Am I/Is he/Are you ...? Short answers: Yes, I am. No, I'm not. Yes, she is. No, she isn't. Yes, they are. No, they aren't. Question words with be: What's your address? How old are they?
parts: Qisqa javoblar (Yes, I am. No, she isn't.)

title: Possessive adjectives (all)
uz: Egalik olmoshlari: my, your, his, her, its, our, their
focus: my, your, his, her, its, our, their + noun: This is our school. Their house is big. Its name is Rex.

title: Possessive 's
focus: Name/noun + 's for possession: John's son, Marie's car, my sister's name, the teacher's book. 's can also mean is: he's = he is. Who's = who is.

title: Plural nouns: rules and irregular
focus: -y to -ies (city-cities, country-countries), -es endings, irregular plurals man-men, woman-women, child-children, person-people, foot-feet, tooth-teeth.

title: have / has
focus: I/you/we/they have; he/she/it has. I have a good job. She has a computer. They have two children. (Beginner: positive sentences mainly.)

title: Possessive pronouns: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs
uz: Egalik olmoshlari: mine, yours, hers ... (meniki, seniki)
focus: Possessive pronoun stands alone without a noun, usually at the end: This book is mine. Is this bag yours? The red car is hers. Compare: This is my book (adjective + noun) vs This book is mine (pronoun). Whose ... is this? It's Tom's.

title: Present Simple: I, you, we, they
uz: Present Simple: I, you, we, they
focus: Positive: I like coffee. We live in London. Negative: I don't like ... They don't work ... Questions: Do you like ...? Short answers: Yes, I do. No, I don't. Where do you live?

title: a / an
focus: a before consonant sound (a book, a university), an before vowel sound (an apple, an hour, an engineer). Jobs: He's a doctor. She's an actor. No article with plurals.

title: Adjective + noun
focus: Adjectives come before the noun and do not take -s: a big house, two red cars, an old man, a fast car. With be: The house is big.

title: Present Simple: he, she, it
focus: He works, she lives, it starts. Spelling: -es after s/sh/ch/x/o (goes, watches), consonant+y → -ies (studies), have → has. Negative: doesn't + verb. Questions: Does she ...? Short answers: Yes, she does. No, he doesn't.

title: Adverbs of frequency
uz: Takrorlik ravishlari (always, usually, often, sometimes, never)
focus: always, usually, often, sometimes, never: before the main verb (I always get up at seven) but after be (She is never late).

title: Telling the time
uz: Soat (vaqtni aytish): past, to, quarter, half
focus: What time is it? It's ten o'clock. five past ten, quarter past ten, half past ten, twenty to eleven, quarter to eleven. at + time: at seven o'clock.

title: Prepositions of time: at, in, on
focus: at + clock time / at night / at the weekend; on + days and dates (on Monday, on 5th May); in + months, years, seasons, parts of day (in July, in 2020, in summer, in the morning).

title: Question words
uz: Savol so'zlari (who, what, where, when, why, how, how much, how many)
focus: who, what, where, when, what time, why, how, how much, how many, which with be and Present Simple: Where do you live? When does it start? Why do you like ...? How much is it?

title: Object pronouns
uz: Kelishikdagi olmoshlar (me, you, him, her, it, us, them)
focus: Subject vs object pronouns: I-me, he-him, she-her, we-us, they-them. I like her. She loves him. Can you help me? Listen to them.

title: this / that / these / those
focus: this (near, singular), that (far, singular), these (near, plural), those (far, plural): This is my bag. That's a nice car. These shoes are new. Those children are noisy.

title: There is / There are
focus: There's a / There are some + place: There's a sofa in the living room. There are two bedrooms. Negative: There isn't / There aren't any. Questions: Is there a ...? Are there any ...? How many ... are there? Short answers.

title: some / any; prepositions of place
uz: some / any va joy predloglari (in, on, under, next to)
focus: some in positive sentences, any in negatives and questions with plural nouns: There are some books. There aren't any chairs. Are there any cups? Prepositions in, on, under, next to, near, opposite.
parts: Joy predloglari (in, on, under, next to)

title: was / were
focus: I/he/she/it was, we/you/they were; wasn't/weren't; Was she ...? Were they ...? Short answers. When were you born? I was born in ... Where were you yesterday?

title: Past Simple: irregular verbs
focus: Common irregular past forms: go-went, have-had, see-saw, buy-bought, come-came, get-got, make-made, take-took, eat-ate, leave-left, give-gave, meet-met, say-said, know-knew. Time expressions: yesterday, last week, ago.

title: Past Simple: regular verbs (positive)
focus: Regular verbs + -ed: worked, played, lived, studied, stopped. Spelling: -d after e, consonant+y → -ied, double consonant (stop-stopped). Same form for all persons.

title: Past Simple: questions and negatives
uz: Past Simple: so'roq va inkor (did / didn't)
focus: did/didn't + base verb for all persons: Did you go ...? Yes, I did. No, I didn't. I didn't see him. Where did you go? What did she buy? (not: didn't went)

title: have / do / go + nouns
focus: Collocations: have breakfast/lunch/dinner/a shower/a good time; do homework/the housework/exercise; go shopping/for a walk/on holiday/home/to work. In Present Simple and Past Simple (had, did, went).

title: can / can't
focus: can + base verb for ability and requests, same for all persons, no -s: I can swim. She can't drive. Can you speak French? Yes, I can. No, I can't. Can I ...? Can you help me?

title: Adverbs
focus: Adjective + -ly: quick-quickly, slow-slowly, careful-carefully, easy-easily; irregular: good-well, fast-fast, hard-hard. Adverbs describe verbs: She speaks English well. He drives carefully.

title: would like
focus: I'd like ... / Would you like ...? for polite offers and requests: I'd like a coffee, please. Would you like a sandwich? Yes, please. No, thank you. I'd like to + verb.

title: some / any with countable and uncountable nouns
uz: some / any: sanaladigan va sanalmaydigan otlar
focus: Countable (apples, eggs) vs uncountable (bread, milk, water, money). some in positives and offers (Would you like some tea?), any in negatives and questions. a/an only with singular countable.

title: like and would like
focus: like = always / in general (I like coffee. Do you like swimming?) vs would like = now / a specific time (I'd like a coffee now. Would you like to go swimming tomorrow?).

title: Present Continuous
focus: am/is/are + verb-ing for actions happening now: I'm reading. She's wearing a red dress. They aren't working. What are you doing? Is it raining? Spelling: -ing, e drop (make-making), double consonant (run-running, sit-sitting).

title: Present Simple and Present Continuous
focus: Present Simple for habits and facts (He usually wears jeans. She works in a bank.) vs Present Continuous for now (Today he's wearing a suit. She's working at home today.). Time words: usually, every day vs now, today, at the moment, Look!

title: Future plans: going to
focus: am/is/are going to + verb for future plans and intentions: I'm going to visit my grandmother. She isn't going to work tomorrow. What are you going to do this weekend? Are they going to buy a car? Time: tomorrow, next week, this weekend, soon.
